newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Over 100,000 refugees on move in Tanzania - WFP.
newsitem.headline: Over 100,000 refugees on move in Tanzania - WFP.

text.p: More than 100,000 Rwandan refugees trekked southeast deeper into Tanzania on Saturday in a column some 20 km (12 miles) long, the U.N. World Food Programme said.
A WFP spokesman said WFP staff drove past the column on Saturday heading southeast into the interior of northwest Tanzania from Kitali and Keza refugee camps and the surrounding area.

"The column is some 20 km (12 miles) long so we estimate it is probably more than 100,000 people. They have encountered some Tanzanian checkpoints and were urged to turn back but have not so far done so," said WFP spokeswoman Michelle Quintaglie.
She said the column was apparently made up of people fleeing Kitali and Keza camps and forests in the area who had not left with other refugees in a series of marches into the bush since last Sunday.

Tanzanian troops and police at roadblocks on Friday turned back hundreds of thousands of Rwandan refugees trying to flee deeper into northwestern Tanzania and ordered them back to the area bordering on Rwanda.

Troops sealed off roads to the border and refugee camps on Saturday in preparation for a return of Rwandan refugees to Rwanda. Aid agencies were excluded from the camps, raising fears that force might be used to prompt the refugees to go home.
